title: Ceres Runtime integration exploratory
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Ceres Runtime to explore integration surface for heterogeneous GPU runtimes and a possible channel partnership. Discussed runtime hooks, kernel selection, benchmarks, sample integrations for Redwood Dedicated/Private, and next steps for a technical deep dive and NDA/partner MSA.
action_items: Lena Morales; Send integration matrix + partner one-pager; due 2026-10-07
Jasper Ng; Prep list of kernel-level hooks and sample patch for Ceres runtime; due 2026-10-14
Marco Ricci; Share internal HW topology docs and preferred quantization presets; due 2026-10-11
Priya Kaur; Confirm commercial lead and contracting timeline; due 2026-10-09
next_steps: Schedule technical deep dive (SE-to-SE) week of Oct 12
Exchange NDA and standard partner MSA draft
Run small micro-benchmark (latency + throughput) using 1 model on representative hardware
Share contact for Redwood Partner Ops
header:
Date: 2026-10-04
Time: 10:30 PT / 13:30 ET
Duration: 46 minutes
Recording: Yes
Platform: Zoom
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE); Jasper Ng (Redwood SE); Ivy Chen (Redwood Solutions); Priya Kaur (Ceres); Marco Ricci (Ceres); Ellen Zhou (Ceres); Tomás Alvarez (Ceres)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really excited to kick this off. Uh, quick round of intros before we get into goals, Jasper do you wanna say hi?
[00:00:12] Jasper Ng: Yeah hi all, Jasper - Redwood infra SE, I focus on runtime integration and perf. I'll be the technical lead on our side for the deep dive.
[00:00:24] Priya Kaur: Hi, Priya here, partnerships at Ceres Runtime. We're looking to partner with inference platforms to reach customers who need heterogeneous GPU orchestration.
[00:00:36] Marco Ricci: Marco - I own HW integrations, we do lots of custom kernel work and have a small team doing quantization tooling.
[00:00:44] Ellen Zhou: Ellen - biz dev, curious about GTM and channel rules.
[00:00:49] Lena Morales: Great, thanks. Top-level agenda: 1) Understand Ceres' runtime capabilities and APIs; 2) surface integration points with Redwood Dedicated/Private; 3) perf/benchmark expectations; 4) next steps. Anything to add?
[00:01:05] Tomás Alvarez: Maybe also commercial models, like referral vs reseller - not too deep now but just flagging.
[00:01:12] Lena Morales: Good call, we'll touch that briefly.
[00:01:20] Jasper Ng: I'll start with what we need from a technical standpoint. Redwood's serving runtime expects certain hooks for kernel selection, KV cache management and batching controls. For partners we typically look for: a plugin to register device types, a low-latency transport layer for tensor movement, and ability to run quantized operators.
[00:01:40] Marco Ricci: When you say KV cache, do you mean the transformer key-value cache? We sometimes see that transcribed as K V cash in some notes, ha. Yes that's supported; our runtime exposes cache attach/detach and snapshot APIs.
[00:01:54] Jasper Ng: Perfect, snapshot APIs are exactly what we'd use for warm starts. How does your runtime handle mixed-precision - do you provide FP16 kernels out of the box?
[00:02:05] Marco Ricci: We have FP16 and optimized INT8 paths, but the INT8 is still experimental for some architectures. Our tooling can run per-layer calibration and provides tuning profiles.
[00:02:16] Lena Morales: From Redwood's product side, we want predictable latency SLOs and clear fallbacks. For Dedicated we offer reserved pools; for Private we ship a customer-managed control plane. Integration ideally shouldn't force customers to special-case.
[00:02:33] Priya Kaur: High-level question: do you foresee us needing to change ABI or will it be adapter-based?
[00:02:40] Jasper Ng: Adapter-based is the preferred path. If we can call into your graph executor via a thin shim we can keep our control plane the same and swap in your kernels where appropriate.
[00:02:50] Ellen Zhou: On the commercial front, what's the typical partner revenue split or reseller model you use?
[00:02:56] Lena Morales: We have a few flavors: referral fees for leads, reseller arrangements with margin splits, and in some cases co-sell with joint discounts. We'll loop in partner ops once we have a technical read.
[00:03:11] Marco Ricci: For the kernel selection, do you have expectations about the format? Like PTX, CUDA kernels, or would you accept a vendor-specific binary blob?
[00:03:21] Jasper Ng: Ideally a shared object with a defined C ABI or a gRPC microservice for operator execution. We've taken both approaches in the past; gRPC gives flexibility but adds RPC latency.
[00:03:33] Tomás Alvarez: We prefer the gRPC extension model for portability across devices but we can compile native plugins if needed.
[00:03:40] Lena Morales: Good nuance — that'll factor into perf testing. Speaking of benchmarks, what workloads should we run? Typical Redwood benchmarks include 1) short prompts tight latency (chatty agents), 2) long context throughput for embeddings/rerank, and 3) memory-bound large-model decode.
[00:03:58] Marco Ricci: We can do those. One ask: can you share a small harness so we avoid re-implementing batching logic; sometimes the handshake on streaming and continuous batching trips people up.
[00:04:10] Jasper Ng: Yep, we'll share a mini harness and sample server config. We'll also provide example SLO targets so you can see what we're tuning to.
[00:04:20] Priya Kaur: On the go-to-market side, if this works we could offer bundling for customers that need both the runtime and a Redwood-managed endpoint. Interested in co-marketing.
[00:04:29] Ellen Zhou: That would be great, we have partners in Europe where our presence is stronger.
[00:04:34] Lena Morales: One thing to flag: security/compliance. For Private deployments, customers often require SAML/SSO, KMS integrations, and audit logs. Do you have any compliance certifications or common controls?
[00:04:46] Marco Ricci: We don't have SOC 2 currently; it's on the roadmap. We do encrypt at rest with customer keys and have RBAC. We can support KMS hooks.
[00:04:55] Jasper Ng: From Redwood's side, we can run partner code in isolated sandboxes on Dedicated pools, but for Private we expect partners to comply with our partner guidelines. We'll share that doc.
[00:05:07] Marco Ricci: Understood.
[00:05:12] Priya Kaur: Curious about fallback policies — if a kernel isn't compatible, do you automatically fall back to another model variant?
[00:05:18] Jasper Ng: Yes, our smart routing supports fallbacks to compatible model variants or different hardware tiers. We can route by policy: latency-first or cost-first.
[00:05:28] Tomás Alvarez: How do you measure per-token cost in distributed setups? Sometimes accounting across nodes is messy.
[00:05:34] Lena Morales: We have token-level breakdowns and per-route cost attribution in the Console. For Dedicated customers we also expose token chargebacks for capacity units.
[00:05:45] Priya Kaur: Anything we should avoid implementing?
[00:05:48] Jasper Ng: Avoid stateful side-effects in operator calls, i.e., don't write to global filesystems. Keep operators stateless or manage state through provided APIs (snapshot/cache).
[00:05:59] Marco Ricci: Noted.
[00:06:05] Lena Morales: Let's pick some concrete first deliverables: 1) exchange NDA and partner MSA; 2) exchange integration matrix and sample harness; 3) run a micro-benchmark with a small LLM and share results. Is that accurate?
[00:06:18] Priya Kaur: Yes.
[00:06:21] Ellen Zhou: One operational question: do you support on-prem air-gapped installs? Several of our customers demand it.
[00:06:28] Jasper Ng: We have a Private deployment that supports air-gapped on-prem with an appliance-style bundle. The control plane is customer-managed in that setup.
[00:06:36] Marco Ricci: Then we'll need to know the OS footprint and container images allowed.
[00:06:41] Jasper Ng: We'll include the image manifest and system requirements in the tech pack.
[00:06:47] Priya Kaur: On timelines, if we started the micro-benchmark next week, how long until we get results?
[00:06:53] Jasper Ng: For a small LLM perf run it's typically 5–7 business days including setup and iterations.
[00:07:00] Tomás Alvarez: Do you have preferred metrics? We usually report p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, and GPU util.
[00:07:06] Lena Morales: Yes, p50/p95, tail latency, throughput, and cost per token are the main ones. Also memory footprint.
[00:07:13] Marco Ricci: We'll include those.
[00:07:16] Ellen Zhou: Quick question about references—do you have existing partners doing similar integrations we could talk to?
[00:07:22] Lena Morales: We do; I can share a couple of partner references — one who integrated a custom runtime and another who did an on-prem pairing.
[00:07:30] Priya Kaur: That would help.
[00:07:33] Jasper Ng: On the technical deep dive, we should plan for an SE-to-SE call with kernel engineers. Expecting 60–90 minutes with a whiteboard and possibly screen share of runbooks.
[00:07:44] Marco Ricci: Sounds good. I'll schedule our kernel folks.
[00:07:48] Lena Morales: Before we wrap, any blockers we should surface?
[00:07:52] Tomás Alvarez: Maybe legal — we prefer custom MSA negotiation windows, but that's fine. Also, we need to confirm support for some of the older Ampere-like devices we still run.
[00:08:02] Jasper Ng: We support Ampere and Hopper families; we'll validate exact micro-arch compatibility during benching.
[00:08:08] Priya Kaur: That addresses our main concerns.
[00:08:11] Lena Morales: Great — recap and next steps: Lena to send partner one-pager + integration matrix, Jasper to send sample harness and schedule SE deep dive, Marco to share HW topology, Priya to confirm contracting lead. We'll set the deep dive for week of Oct 12. Anything else?
[00:08:28] Ellen Zhou: Please include contact for partner ops.
[00:08:31] Lena Morales: Will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[00:08:36] Priya Kaur: Thanks, bye.
[00:08:38] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and stutters, product names sometimes transcribed as Redwood Dedicated/Redwood Private inconsistently. Some punctuation and capitalization are auto-generated.

Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.ai/partners/integration-matrix (sample link), https://drive.redwood.ai/bench-harness/mini-harness.zip (sample harness link)
notes: Spoke about adapter vs native plugin, gRPC vs ABI, compliance needs (KMS, SSO), and initial micro-benchmark plan. Low friction expected technically; legal/MSA and SOC2 roadmap were the main commercial considerations.
